text: You dug a pool, filled it with one million dollars, and put the strongest armor in the world on top. Will the I.R.S. find it? In real life, they don't need a satellite. Day one, you sleep like a king on top of your million. Day two, you buy a brand new truck. But your neighbor saw everything: the excavator, the cash, and the steel lid. And the I.R.S. pays rewards for tips. So they open your tax return. It says you made almost nothing. A pool full of money and no income? That's a giant red flag. Because the I.R.S. doesn't care where you hide money. It cares where the money came from. Two weeks later: black S.U.V.s, police cars, and agents at your door. The whole street is watching. They walk you to the backyard. One agent points at the lid. Open it. You type the code. Wrong. You try again. Wrong. You built the strongest armor in the world, and you forgot the code. Now you're in a gray room downtown. Give us the code. You swear you don't remember. They ask again, and again. Nobody believes you. Here's the real lesson. Keeping cash at home is legal. Hiding the income it came from is tax evasion: up to five years in prison. And on top of the tax, the fraud penalty alone is seventy-five percent. And the lid? They just bring a bigger excavator. Your million comes out, one strap at a time, straight into evidence bags. So, pay the tax and sleep well, or keep the pool and pray? Comment TAX or POOL.
